title: Why 'ok.' can start a fight
series: The invisible rules of human behavior

scenes.say: One text. Two completely different messages.
You ask a simple question. They reply, okay, with a full stop. And suddenly you're wondering what you did wrong.
Text strips away the voice, the pauses, the face. Your brain fills the gap.
In one study, senders expected their tone to come through seventy-eight percent of the time. Email readers got it right fifty-six percent. Close to chance.
Another study found text replies ending in a full stop were rated less sincere. The same handwritten note wasn't.
So before you react, ask: is it their tone, or my mind filling the gap?
